methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multi-institutional genomic analysis using GENIE database (423 cSCC samples from 406 patients, 16 centers). Harmonized sequencing data across panels. Clear variant filtering (VAF ≥5%, depth ≥100×). Appropriate statistical methods (chi-squared, Fisher's exact, FDR correction for multiple comparisons). Limitations: tumor-only sequencing (no matched normal), cross-institutional platform heterogeneity acknowledged but not fully corrected, limited clinical outcome data.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective genomic database analysis. Identifies recurrent mutations (TP53 83.5%, NOTCH1 56.3%, etc.) relevant to cSCC biology. However, no outcome associations, no treatment response data, limited translational validation.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE adherence adequate: objectives, cohort selection, statistical methods detailed. Gaps: limited clinical annotation in GENIE, no treatment/outcome follow-up, pre-registration not mentioned. Data source (GENIE) is public.

novelty_literature.justification: cSCC genomic studies published; this analysis consolidates mutation frequencies across institutions. Adds detail (hotspot characterization, co-occurrence patterns) but primarily confirmatory of prior findings (TP53, NOTCH1, CDKN2A).

writing_presentation.justification: Methods well-documented. Results include lollipop plots for mutation hotspots and co-occurrence heatmaps. However, limited discussion of therapeutic implications; largely descriptive of mutation landscape.

key_strengths: Large multi-institutional harmonized genomic cohort (423 samples, 16 centers) providing robust mutation frequency estimates
Comprehensive mutation characterization including hotspots, copy-number alterations, and statistically tested co-occurrence patterns
FDR correction applied for multiple comparisons; identified race/sex-based patterns in low-frequency alterations
key_concerns: No clinical outcome or treatment response data limits therapeutic implications
Tumor-only sequencing without matched normal limits somatic vs germline distinction
Limited discussion of pathway implications or mechanism; primarily descriptive genomics without functional validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Comprehensive descriptive genomics study confirming established cSCC drivers. Tier 3 appropriate for cohort genomic characterization lacking outcome associations.
